props.name: voiceActive

props.name: onActiveIndexChange

props.name: zoom

props.name: initialZoom

props.name: onZoomChange
props.doc: called on every pinch, double-tap and settle

props.name: zoomable
props.doc: whether pinch and double-tap magnify at all. Off leaves the pager and the dismiss intact.

props.name: loading
props.doc: the photos are on their way: the grid holds their space with skeleton frames

props.name: placeholderCount
props.doc: how many frames that skeleton grid holds

props.name: disabled
props.doc: the grid stands and reads, and opens nothing

props.name: container
props.doc: where the lightbox opens. `viewport` puts it on Base's own Layer, over everything. `parent` opens it inside the gallery's own box — for a viewer that belongs to one pane of a split screen, and for a reference page that has to show the open state in place. A `parent` lightbox is as tall as the gallery's own box, so give that box a height.

props.name: reference

props.doc: any CSS length; a number is read as px

props.name: grow

props.name: children
props.doc: THE NESTING SLOT. A sub-scenario renders full-fidelity inside a skeleton parent, so you can see exactly where in the undecided page the decided moment lives. Give a ghost children and it yields its ground to them: the fill drops, the geometry stays, and pointer events come back for the real component inside.

props.name: label
props.doc: ROCOTO: the STOP, not a string. Base takes `label: string` and centres it; the driver's row carries the customer, the address and the amount to collect, and that whole object is what the thumb pushes. A node, so a stop is composed out of the kit like anything else.

props.name: completedLabel
props.doc: ROCOTO: what the row says once it has been swept — a time, a name, whatever the surface knows afterwards. Base repeats the label; a driver already read it, and what they want now is the receipt for the act they just performed.

props.name: threshold
props.doc: how far the hand must travel before the row commits. `door` is the driver's half.

props.name: size
props.doc: ROCOTO: `large` is the gloved row I3 draws.

props.name: size

props.doc: the accessible name. Absent, the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers — which is right beside a product name it would otherwise read twice.

props.doc: ROCOTO: one quantity per part, in the order the parts stand. Two parts is one boundary, three parts is two. Anything that does not sum to `total` is normalised on the way in, so a caller can never hold a division that does not add up.

props.name: step
props.doc: the granularity the boundary steps through. Default 1.

props.name: minPart
props.doc: ROCOTO: the smallest a part may be dragged to. A part at 0 is a part that should be removed rather than emptied, so the floor stops the control short of a lie.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disable control from being changed.

props.name: marks
props.doc: Display a mark at each step.

props.doc: Function to change the numeric value to a user friendly value. Also applied to the ticks.

props.name: captions
props.doc: ROCOTO: a second line under a part's name — the cost that part was bought at.

props.doc: Handler for events on trigger element, each time the boundary moves.

props.name: onFinalChange

props.name: value
props.doc: the signature the pad shows — pass it to control the pad, `null` for none

props.name: defaultValue

props.name: typedNameValue

props.doc: «units», «kg», «cases» — shares the number's line, always

props.name: decimals
